//: This directory only. It declares what these files already are — ES modules — so that Vite's
config loader stops reporting them as CommonJS carrying ESM syntax.
All three packages' vitest.config.ts reach determinism.ts through their own
tests/determinism.ts re-export, which pulls a REPO-ROOT file into the config bundle. The root
package.json has no "type", so Vite classified these as CommonJS and printed a
configLoader: 'native' incompatibility notice on every test gate. Vite's only other lever is
VITE_CONFIG_NATIVE_IGNORE_WARNING, which suppresses the message rather than answering it, and
scripts/ci/report.mjs counts that notice into warnings.compiler, which is ratcheted at zero.
SCOPED HERE, NEVER AT THE ROOT. Adding "type": "module" to the root package.json was tried
and is measurably wrong: Playwright loads e2e/*.ts through a CommonJS require path and those
files use __dirname deliberately (see the note at e2e/helpers.ts:493), so e2e and a11y both
died with 'ReferenceError: __dirname is not defined in ES module scope'; and CodeQL's own
vendored parser wrapper is a CommonJS .js file under .cache/, which the root package scope
reaches, so sast died with 'exports is not defined in ES module scope' as well.
THREE CommonJS callers import this directory across that boundary, and all three are exercised
by the e2e and a11y gates on every push: playwright.config.ts:6 (the CONFIG load, whose failure
shape is the silent 'No tests found'), e2e/helpers.ts:5, and e2e/start-server.ts:5.
THE INVARIANT THAT ARRANGEMENT DEPENDS ON, and nothing else pins it: NO FILE IN THIS DIRECTORY
MAY TAKE A TOP-LEVEL AWAIT. require() of an ESM module works only while the module graph is
synchronous; one top-level await turns every one of those three imports into
ERR_REQUIRE_ASYNC_MODULE. s3Server.ts, which stands a container up, is where somebody will
reach for one.
